transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I, um, I hope I'm doing this right. 

I'm here because... well, things at work have been a little complicated, and I really don't want to sound unreasonable or unprofessional. I work in mathematical sciences, and recently... well, I'm pretty sure the people on this environmental modeling contract we have are tracking my revisions. It really seems like they're planting errors in the datasets, just to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. 

I hate to even say it out loud because I know how it might sound, and I don't want you to think poorly of me. My wife and the junior analysts, they keep telling me it’s just normal version-control mistakes, but... I don't know. Am I explaining that clearly enough for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Aside from these concerns about the datasets, have you ever heard voices, whispering, or other sounds that no one else seemed to hear?

No, no, I haven't experienced anything like that. I mean, occasionally I might think I hear my name being called if it's noisy, but nothing out of the ordinary, you know? Just the normal kind of thing anyone might experience. 

I really try to keep a level head about things, and I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm... well, that I'm hearing things that aren't there. I'm just very focused on the data and the work. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the way you need me to.
Have you experienced similar feelings of people working against you or trying to undermine you in previous jobs or relationships, or is this the first time?

Oh, no... no, definitely not. I've been doing this for a long time, and I've always prided myself on having very good, very professional relationships with my colleagues. I mean, sure, you have the usual minor disagreements over a project's direction here and there, but never... never anything like this where I felt someone was actively trying to, well, undermine me. 

I really wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who just goes around blaming other people for my own mistakes. I take my job very seriously, and I've always been a team player. So, yes, this is really the first time I've ever dealt with a situation quite like this. It's just this specific contract. 

I hope... I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you a clear picture of my history, Doctor. Am I giving you the kind of background you need?
How long have you felt that colleagues on this contract are intentionally planting errors to undermine your work?

Well, um... I guess it's been about two months now. I mean, I didn't want to jump to any conclusions right away, of course. I always try to give people the benefit of the doubt. But over the last two months, it's just become... well, I'm quite certain now that they are tracking my revisions and putting those errors in. 

I know two months might sound like a long time to let something like this go on without saying anything, and I hope you don't think I'm just being paranoid or... or difficult to work with. I just wanted to be absolutely sure before I even brought it up to my wife or anyone else. Does that seem like a reasonable timeframe to you, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you accurate information.
When this all started about two months ago, did it begin abruptly over a couple of days, or did it build up gradually?

Well, um, I suppose it was more of a gradual thing. I didn't just wake up one morning and think, oh, they're out to get me. I'm really not that kind of person, you know? I try to be very rational about my work. 

At first, I just thought I was making silly mistakes, or maybe the software was glitching. But then, over a few weeks, the pattern just became too obvious to ignore. I really took my time to analyze it before coming to any conclusions, because I know how it sounds. I wouldn't want you to think I'm the type to just snap and start pointing fingers. 

So, yes, it built up slowly as I noticed more and more discrepancies. I hope that's the kind of detail you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it clearly so you can see I'm being logical about this.
Over these past couple of months, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or hopeless?

Oh, no, no. I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, it's been a bit stressful, naturally, trying to figure out what's happening with my data... but I'm certainly not depressed or hopeless. 

I've always tried to maintain a very positive, productive outlook, you know? I still get up every morning ready to tackle my work and do a good job. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of person who just gives up or lets things get them down like that. I'm handling the situation as best as I can, keeping my chin up and staying focused on the math. 

Is... is that what you were asking, Doctor? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right kind of information. I hope I'm not painting the wrong picture here.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions or noticed any changes in your physical health recently?

Well, um... no, actually. I've always been very fortunate with my physical health. I try to take really good care of myself, you know, keeping a steady routine and all that so I can stay sharp for my work. I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm neglecting myself just because of the stress with the contract. 

So, no, I haven't been diagnosed with any medical conditions, and I haven't noticed any changes in my body or anything like that. Everything is running just fine on that front. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a complete picture, Doctor. Is that the sort of information you needed for your notes?
Have you ever felt that thoughts were being put into your head from the outside?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I mean, my thoughts are entirely my own. I'm a mathematician, after all, so my mind is my most important tool. I pride myself on having a very clear, independent way of thinking. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm... well, that I'm losing control of my own mind or anything like that. That sounds quite frightening, honestly, but it's not something I've ever experienced. All the conclusions I've come to about the data and the contract, they're based on my own analysis, my own deductions. 

So, no, no outside thoughts being put in there. I hope that makes sense? I just want to reassure you that I'm completely in charge of my own faculties, Doctor. Is that... does that answer your question satisfactorily?
